exposure: type of cesarean section (emergency vs. elective)
cohort: 161 women over the age of 18 who underwent either elective or emergency Cesarean sections.
finding: The relationship between the type of cesarean section and post-traumatic symptom levels was fully mediated by the sense of internal control, where emergency C-sections led to lower internal control, which in turn correlated negatively with post-traumatic symptom levels.
mod_finding: Emergency cesarean sections were associated with lower levels of internal control, which mediated higher post-traumatic symptoms compared to elective cesarean sections.
